title: Agentic AI in the Software Development Lifecycle: Architecture, Empirical Evidence, and the Reshaping of Software Engineering
key_points: Agentic AI systems operate at the level of repositories, features, or algorithms, a shift from earlier line- or function-level code completion tools like GitHub Copilot.
The paper proposes a six-layer reference architecture (L0–L5) for agentic software engineering systems and contrasts the traditional SDLC with an Agentic SDLC (A-SDLC).
SWE-bench Verified resolution rates rose from 1.96% (October 2023) to 78.4% (April 2026) according to the paper, while non-agentic RAG systems plateaued near 20%.
Reported productivity gains range from 13.6% to 55.8% across controlled studies, and 49% of jobs in Anthropic's sample saw Claude used for at least a quarter of their tasks.

The paper argues the central object of inquiry has shifted from code generation to delegated execution under human supervision, and identifies five open problems: evaluation, governance, technical debt, skill redistribution, and the economics of attention.
unclear_sections: Figure 5 (capability–autonomy plane) has overlapping labels for Codex CLI and Jules, and the Claude label is cut off at the page edge, making some positions hard to read.
Some figure and table values (such as Table 2 SWE-bench percentages) are marked as approximate in the source, and the paper's Figure 2 and Figure 3 labels are small and partly obscured.
